title: A Long Way Home
author: Saroo Brierley with Larry Buttrose
target_audience: Individuals drawn to narratives of childhood survival
Fans of cross-cultural human interest journeys
People interested in the impact of new technology on personal lives
core_themes: The power and limits of memory
Impact of technology in reconnecting families
primary_purpose: To recount Saroo Brierley's incredible journey from getting lost as a young child in India, surviving alone, being adopted by an Australian family, and eventually using new digital tools to search for and reunite with his birth family.

structure_format.organization: Sequentially narrates Saroo’s childhood in India, separation from his family, survival in Calcutta, adoption in Australia, search for origins, and eventual reunion

key_concepts_lessons: The experience of displacement and longing for one’s roots can span decades and shape identity.
Adoption is complex, bringing both loving new opportunities and deep questions about origin.
Childhood memories, even fragmented, can be powerful anchors for adult identity and motivation.
Advances in technology, such as Google Earth, can make extraordinary personal searches possible.
Resilience, hope, and persistence can lead to healing and belonging.
notable_features: Interweaves themes of poverty, loss, cultural adaptation, and global technology
Gives voice to both biological and adoptive families
Compelling blend of suspense, emotion, and self-discovery
cultural_historical_context: Set against the backdrop of 1980s-2000s India and Australia, the memoir highlights challenges faced by street children in India and evolving practices in intercountry adoption. It also illustrates how digital mapping technology began to profoundly affect personal search efforts in the 21st century.
reception_impact: International bestseller, translated into numerous languages
Critically acclaimed for its heartfelt narrative and hope-inspiring message
Praised by adoption advocates, social workers, and general readers alike
Helped inspire further awareness about missing children and family reunification
Film adaptation ('Lion') received multiple Academy Award nominations
comparable_titles: The Boy Who Was Raised as a Dog by Bruce D. Perry and Maia Szalavitz
The Glass Castle by Jeannette Walls
Finding Family: My Search for Roots and the Secrets in My DNA by Richard Hill
